criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies that Paragraph 7(b) lacks a requirement for in-house counsel to be identified by name
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup revises 7(b) to require Designated In-House Counsel be identified by name, title and responsibilities, with comment flagging named designation as client priority #2(a), identifying the gap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies that Paragraph 7(b) lacks a procedure for the producing party to object to specific in-house counsel
criteria_results.reasoning: New 7(e) adds a five-business-day objection right; comment identifies it as client priority #2(b), addressing the absence of any objection procedure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies that Paragraph 7(b) lacks a competitive wall requirement for in-house counsel
criteria_results.reasoning: New 7(d) Competitive Decision-Making restriction with comment labeling it the client's 'competitive wall' priority, identifying the missing screen.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes named-designation procedure with objection right for in-house counsel
criteria_results.reasoning: 7(b) requires identification by name 5 business days before access and 7(e) gives a 5-business-day objection right.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes restriction excluding in-house counsel with pricing/sales responsibilities
criteria_results.reasoning: 7(d) excludes in-house counsel with direct pricing, sales or operational responsibilities in the Overlap Markets, defined in 2(m) as Portland-Vancouver, Seattle-Tacoma, Boise and Sacramento.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies problem with sharing to DOJ/State AGs without notice
criteria_results.reasoning: Comments on Para. 14 discuss the absence of prior notice (Staff 'non-negotiable' as to prior notice) and add notice alternatives in 14(d), identifying the issue.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes prior written notice requirement before sharing with DOJ/State AGs
criteria_results.reasoning: The markup expressly declines to propose the 10-business-day prior notice; Alternative A is only best-efforts prior notice with no defined period, and Alternative B is after-the-fact.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes receiving agency must agree to be bound by protective order terms
criteria_results.reasoning: 14(b) requires the Commission to obtain the receiving agency's written agreement to maintain confidentiality consistent with the order's tiers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes right to seek court order preventing disclosure to DOJ/State AGs
criteria_results.reasoning: No provision gives the producing party a right to seek a court order or other relief to prevent disclosure to DOJ or state AGs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes FTC Staff indicated sharing provision is 'non-negotiable'
criteria_results.reasoning: Margin comment states 'Heller: Para. 14 is "non-negotiable" as to prior notice.'

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes alternative/compromise language for the sharing provision
criteria_results.reasoning: 14(d) offers bracketed Alternative A (best-efforts prior notice) and Alternative B (after-the-fact notice within 5 business days) as compromises, plus the 14(b) written agreement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies that 'conclusion of the investigation' is undefined
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup adds a definition of 'Conclusion of the Investigation' (2(j)) used in 19(a), with comment noting Heller called the undefined trigger a 'fair point', identifying the ambiguity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes specific definition of 'conclusion of the investigation'
criteria_results.reasoning: 2(j) defines conclusion via closing letter, consent order, abandonment/outside date, and addresses subsequent Part 3/13(b) proceedings.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Addresses what happens to materials if administrative litigation follows
criteria_results.reasoning: 19(d) suspends return/destruction during any Subsequent Proceeding, with the 60-day clock starting after final resolution.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies absence of FRE 502(d) reference in clawback provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment on 16(e) responds to the 502(d) question and explains the Commission cannot enter a 502(d) order, identifying the missing 502(d) protection.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Explains significance of missing FRE 502(d) — waiver risk in other proceedings
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment explains the order cannot by itself bind non-parties in later litigation without a federal-court 502(d) order, i.e., waiver risk elsewhere.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes FRE 502(d) order or equivalent language
criteria_results.reasoning: 16(e) commits parties to jointly move for a FRE 502(d) order in any 13(b) action and an equivalent ALJ order in Part 3.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies risk of FTC economist rotation to private consulting
criteria_results.reasoning: Comments on 2(f) and 12(c) flag the economist rotation concern and that existing rules do not restrict a former economist's later use of commercial data in private consulting.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes individual acknowledgment forms or post-separation restrictions for FTC Staff
criteria_results.reasoning: 12(c) individual Staff certification and 12(d) departure notification within 12 months are proposed, plus a bracketed post-separation restriction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies that HC tier definition excludes structured data/financial models
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment notes the 'documents'-only formulation of 3(b) arguably leaves structured data outside the HC tier.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes expanded HC definition to include structured data and databases
criteria_results.reasoning: 3(b) expanded to Documents and Structured Data including pricing databases, route/lane cost data, customer profitability, financial models and spreadsheets.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Project Atlas and Cascade profitability data as examples
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup and memo reference Project Atlas and Cascade's customer-level profitability data as materials to be covered.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies 10 business day challenge deadline as unreasonably short
criteria_results.reasoning: The 18(c) comment does not identify the 10-business-day deadline as unreasonably short given the ~1.88M-document volume; it frames the extension as mainly benefiting challengers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes extending challenge deadline to approximately 20 business days
criteria_results.reasoning: 18(c) extends the motion deadline to twenty (20) business days.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes designations remain in effect during challenge pendency
criteria_results.reasoning: New 18(f) provides designations remain in full force pending resolution of a challenge.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies lack of provision for PE sponsor third-party materials
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment identifies the gap for Ridgeline-originated materials produced from Cascade's files and lack of independent designation rights, addressed by Originating Third Party provisions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes independent third-party designation rights for sources of produced materials
criteria_results.reasoning: Para. 25(a) lets an Originating Third Party designate or increase designation of its own materials.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes notice to third parties before redesignation or disclosure of their materials
criteria_results.reasoning: Para. 25 gives Originating Third Parties notice of production, challenges, subpoenas, agency sharing and public disclosure of their materials.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: References Ridgeline-specific materials (fund performance, LP communications, IRR)
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup 3(c)(vi)/2(l) and memo reference fund-level performance data, investor/LP communications, investment committee memoranda and valuation models.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies absence of treatment for confidential info in subsequent litigation
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment on new Para. 23 identifies the need for a bridge provision for Part 3 or 13(b) proceedings, which the FTC draft lacked.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes bridge provision for subsequent administrative/judicial proceedings
criteria_results.reasoning: Para. 23 provides designations survive an administrative complaint/13(b) action and parties will negotiate a supplemental protective order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies lack of conflicts check for experts/consultants
criteria_results.reasoning: New 8(d)-(e) conflicts disclosure with comment citing precedent and Heller, identifying that Para. 8 lacked a competitor-conflict screen.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes conflicts-check disclosure and objection right for experts
criteria_results.reasoning: 8(d) requires 24-month competitor engagement disclosure, 8(e) a 5-business-day objection, and 8(f) a forward-looking restriction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes third-tier 'Attorneys Eyes Only' or equivalent super-tier
criteria_results.reasoning: New AEO third tier (3(c), 9A) limited to three named outside attorneys per side and excluding all experts absent consent or order.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies Project Atlas and Cascade profitability data as candidates for third tier
criteria_results.reasoning: Markup bracketed 3(c)(i) and memo identify Project Atlas and Cascade customer-level profitability data as third-tier candidates.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References market practice supporting three-tier systems in merger investigations
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Crestline/Durango (Mergers IV) and Thornfield/Beckett (Mergers II) precedent supporting a three-tier system.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies no provision for derivative materials incorporating confidential info
criteria_results.reasoning: Comment on Para. 24 notes that without it an expert white paper synthesizing AEO data could circulate at a lower tier, identifying the derivative-materials gap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes derivative materials provision with automatic highest-designation rule
criteria_results.reasoning: Para. 24 assigns Derivative Material the highest tier applicable to any source material.

criteria_results.title: Marginal comments include legal/practical basis for each proposed change
criteria_results.reasoning: Margin comments explain practical risks and legal bases (e.g., U.S. Steel/Brown Bag, FRE 502, 18a(h), gun-jumping).

criteria_results.title: Marginal comments reference FTC Staff's signaled flexibility from April 8 call
criteria_results.reasoning: Many comments cite Heller/Munoz positions from the April 8 call, including flexibility on challenge deadline and conclusion definition and 'non-negotiable' on Para. 14.

criteria_results.title: Marginal comments assess likelihood of Staff acceptance (high/medium/low)
criteria_results.reasoning: Comments give qualitative acceptance assessments ('easy win', 'expect Staff to reject', 'medium difficulty', 'Expect pushback').

criteria_results.title: Cover memo proposes alternatives where Staff signaled resistance

criteria_results.title: Cover memo addresses protection for Project Atlas board materials
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo addresses Project Atlas protection via third tier and public-filing notice.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo addresses concern about FTC economists rotating to private consulting
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo addresses FTC staff rotation and a former economist's later use of commercial data.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo addresses risk of sensitive pricing data disclosure to competitors
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo addresses inter-party leakage risk of pricing/bid strategy and customer data between direct competitors.

criteria_results.title: Cover memo addresses Ridgeline Capital Partners' concerns
